Marie / Aditya / Lauren — thanks for the redline and the heads-up. We've reviewed internally and propose the following compromise points (summary below; full text attached as a redline pdf). Please find the proposed language in Redwood_Proposal_IP_Split_20260503.pdf.

Summary of proposed compromise:
1) Scope split: Redwood will defend & indemnify SpectraData for third-party IP claims to the extent the claim alleges infringement arising from: (a) modifications made solely by Redwood, or (b) model outputs that can be shown (by preponderance) to derive from Redwood-origin model training artifacts (not customer-supplied content). SpectraData will defend & indemnify for claims arising from customer-provided data, prompts, or instructions.

2) Defense control: Redwood requests lead defense control for claims within Redwood's indemnity bucket, with SpectraData given reasonable participation rights and the right to select local counsel at its expense. For mixed claims, parties will meet in good faith to propose split counsel arrangements; if no agreement within 21 days, Redwood may assume defense subject to reservation of rights.

3) Cap & insurance floor: Contract cap for 3rd-party IP claims = greater of $2,000,000 or 2x the prior 12 months' fees (consistent with the deal size). Insurance offsets allowed but may not reduce Redwood's residual exposure below $500,000 (i.e., minimum residual cap to protect interests).

4) Notice & cure: Prompt notice required; claimant's written notice to the other party within 30 days of receiving claim. Where a cure opportunity exists (e.g., takedown, license purchase), SpectraData will be given 30 days to cure non-material issues before indemnity obligations accelerate.

5) Evidence & escrow: For claims tied to training data provenance, we propose an evidence escalation process (shared bucket accessible to both parties) and an initial escrow hold for critical artifacts for 90 days post-notice to preserve forensic proof.

6) Insurance requirements: Redwood will provide COI listing carriers and limits; we are open to mutualizing certain endorsements for the Order Form. Procurement checklist (attached previously) specifies required fields.

We believe this gives SpectraData strong protection for customer-provided content while protecting Redwood from open-ended exposure due to model output uncertainty. If you agree in principle, let's schedule a 30-minute call to finalize the language and timing for procurement deliverables.

Regards,
Kimberly Park
